messages:
Priya (Support): FYI — customer ACME reported intermittent 429s and billing anomalies after they migrated a batch job to call our text-generation endpoint in bursts. They say it works for a few minutes then starts getting 429 + "quota_exhausted" errors. Ticket 5872. Can eng-platform confirm whether this is quota exhaustion vs rate-limit?

Eli (Eng-Platform): Hmm, likely token- or request-based throttling. Do you have repro info from the customer? pattern (concurrency, batch size, tokens per request)? Also which plan (free/standard/enterprise)?

Priya (Support): They were on Standard, hitting the /v1/generate endpoint with a scheduled job: 8 parallel workers, each sending 10 requests/s for ~2m bursts every 10 minutes. Each request ~2k tokens output. Headers show 200 for a few min, then 429 with body: {\"error\":\"quota_exhausted\", \"detail\":\"tokens per minute exceeded\"}. They saw billing credit usage spike too.

Jorge (SRE): Thanks. That behavior matches a token-bucket quota: sustained rate okay up to limit, but after cumulative tokens exceed TPM, requests fail until refill. Bursts consume bucket capacity quickly. Could also be per-key aggregate across their multiple API keys?

Eli (Eng-Platform): We should run a focused internal load test in staging to find the knee for RPM/TPM and burst sizes for the Standard profile. I'll spin up a small vegeta script and a token-emulation test. Quick plan: replicate their pattern (8 workers, bursts every 10m) and also run steady-state and short high-burst tests to observe p95 latency and 429 ramp.

Priya (Support): Also they reported auth refresh failures around the same time — some 401s interleaved before 429. Could be our auth rate-limits on token verification (OIDC introspection) under load?

Eli (Eng-Platform): Good catch. We'll include auth call tracing. If token verification load spikes, it could cause upstream latency, increasing request duration and causing clients to retry and worsen the burst. We'll instrument introspection endpoint RPS in the test.

loadbot: Scheduled load test job #load-20260312-01 in staging at 03:00 UTC. Config attached.

Priya (Support): Thanks. Can you also provide repro steps we can give the customer to isolate whether it's our quota or something in their orchestration (eg retries)? Need a minimal script they can run.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Repro snippet for support to hand to customer (curl loop):

```bash
# single-threaded burst repro — replace $KEY and $URL
for i in {1..400}; do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"hello","max_tokens":2000}' \
    $URL/v1/generate &
  if (( i % 50 == 0 )); then sleep 0.5; fi
done
wait
```

This will send a concentrated burst; ask them to capture the sequence of HTTP codes and the timestamps. If 429s start after X requests/time, that's their effective bucket.

Maya (Customer Success): Also note we saw billing knock-on effects: their usage meter jumped then credits applied and then billing alerts fired. We should ensure billing metrics use the same token accounting as throttling to avoid confusing customers.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Agreed — we have to keep charging metric consistent with enforcement. For the load test I ran a couple quick experiments in staging (results below).

loadbot: attach results: ~/artifacts/load-20260312-01/summary.log

Eli (Eng-Platform): Summary (staging small instance, current Standard profile throttles):
- Steady test: 8 workers, 5 rps each, 0 burst => sustained 40 rps, p95 latency 180ms, 0 429s over 30m.
- Burst test A: 8 workers, 50 rps each for 90s (concurrent bursts) => ~17% requests returned 429 after ~60s; p95 latency climbed to 1.2s before 429s started.
- Burst test B (token heavy): same burst but max_tokens=2000 => bucket exhausted in ~45s; 429s at ~45s, then 429s persisted ~120s until refill.

Observations: current Standard TPM is effectively set at ~3,000,000 tokens/min across their account config in staging (we cap per-account). The burst capacity (bucket size) is small relative to large-output requests which explains the quick exhaustion. Also auth introspection calls increased by ~30% during bursts but stayed under threshold and not the primary failure cause.

Jorge (SRE): Useful. From a resilience perspective: we should allow short bursts but fail fast with Retry-After and a clear quota_exceeded reason. Recommend adding a client-visible X-Quota-Remaining header too.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Proposed sane defaults (for Hosted API Standard tier) — these are conservative starting points we can tune after larger load runs: 
- Requests per minute (RPM): 120 RPM per key (2 rps sustained).
- Tokens per minute (TPM): 300k TPM per key.
- Burst (token-bucket capacity): allow burst capacity up to 3x refill rate (i.e., capacity = 3 * TPM/60 = 3 * (300k/60) = 15k tokens immediate burst).
- Short absolute request-burst cap: 40 requests in a 10s window (to avoid stampeding short requests).

Rationale: 120 RPM gives consistent low-latency experience for interactive apps, 300k TPM handles a few mid-sized generations per minute, and a 3x burst allows natural spikes but not sustained abuse. For free-tier, drop TPM to 50k and RPM 30. For enterprise/dedicated, either lift or disable these defaults and rely on reserved capacity policies.

Priya (Support): Those defaults seem reasonable for preventing noisy neighbor impact. How do we expose them to customers and show applied limits when they hit them? Need messaging for support KB and the error payload.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Error format proposal (already used in tests):
```json
{
  "error": "quota_exhausted",
  "type": "tokens_per_minute",
  "retry_after": 74,
  "quota_remaining_tokens": 0
}
```
We'll also add headers: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Limit, Retry-After. Add a dashboard panel for 429 rate and top offending API keys.

Maya (Customer Success): Also propose automated guidance: when Support sees repeated 429s, suggest escalation playbook: 1) ask for concurrency pattern and token sizes, 2) run our support repro script, 3) suggest changes (reduce parallelism, increase inter-burst spacing, lower max_tokens or move to Dedicated). Include recommended tuning (eg reduce max_tokens to 512, or use streaming to reduce token spikes).

Jorge (SRE): One more engineering note: implement a short-term soft-throttle that returns 202 + progress token for very large jobs that exceed burst but can be queued on Dedicated. That reduces customer retry storms. Might be longer term.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Next steps:
- (Eli) Run expanded load matrix in staging (different token sizes, concurrency, and multi-key aggregation) — target run window tonight.
- (Jorge) Add dashboard panels for 429/Quota metrics and auth-introspection RPS.
- (Support) Priya/Maya draft customer-facing KB + repro snippet and escalation steps.
- (All) Revisit defaults after one week of staged tests.

Priya (Support): I'll update ticket 5872 with the repro snippet and interim guidance and link to this thread. If we see a customer on Standard who needs higher sustained throughput we'll recommend Dedicated.

deploy-bot: deploy staging:rate-limiter-config v2 -> success (timestamp 1710427320)

Eli (Eng-Platform): Deployed v2 rate-limiter config to staging. It applies the proposed default values for Standard. I'll post detailed load artifacts after the full matrix completes.

Priya (Support): Great — thanks everyone. We'll hold on escalations until we confirm with the customer after they run the curl loop.

Maya (Customer Success): I'll proactively message the customer with suggested short-term mitigations (stagger jobs by 30s, cap max_tokens) and offer to coordinate a Dedicated trial if they need predictable sustained throughput.

Eli (Eng-Platform): Post-test note (will paste later): for very token-heavy workloads we should prefer per-route TPM (so embeddings/rerankers don't consume generation token budget).

Jorge (SRE): +1. Also add an alert when any single API key consumes >50% of account TPM for >5m so SRE/support can proactively reach out.

Priya (Support): Thread resolved for now — updating ticket. Thanks all.
